candidates.title: Transformer Quality in Linear Time
candidates.abstract: We revisit the design choices in Transformers, and propose methods to address their weaknesses in handling long sequences. First, we propose a simple layer named gated attention unit, which allows the use of a weaker single-head attention with minimal quality loss. We then propose a linear approximation method complementary to this new layer, which is accelerator-friendly and highly competitive in quality. The resulting model, named FLASH, matches the perplexity of improved Transformers over both short (512) and long (8K) context lengths, achieving training speedups of up to 4.9$\times$ on Wiki-40B and 12.1$\times$ on PG-19 for auto-regressive language modeling, and 4.8$\times$ on C4 for masked language modeling.
candidates.reason: Gated Attention Unitとアクセラレータ親和的な線形注意近似を組み合わせたFLASHを提案し、自己回帰言語モデルで長系列の計算量を線形化する。8K文脈を含む言語モデル評価でTransformer品質を維持しつつ大幅な実行高速化を示しており、長文脈推論効率化へ直接つながるため対象内。
candidates.library_body_check: full_text_checked: 一次論文でGated Attention Unit、線形注意近似、短文脈/8K長文脈の言語モデル評価と実行速度比較を確認。自己回帰推論へ適用可能な線形時間architectureとしてaccept。

candidates.title: Deja Vu: Contextual Sparsity for Efficient LLMs at Inference Time
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) with hundreds of billions of parameters have sparked a new wave of exciting AI applications. However, they are computationally expensive at inference time. Sparsity is a natural approach to reduce this cost, but existing methods either require costly retraining, have to forgo LLM's in-context learning ability, or do not yield wall-clock time speedup on modern hardware. We hypothesize that contextual sparsity, which are small, input-dependent sets of attention heads and MLP parameters that yield approximately the same output as the dense model for a given input, can address these issues. We show that contextual sparsity exists, that it can be accurately predicted, and that we can exploit it to speed up LLM inference in wall-clock time without compromising LLM's quality or in-context learning ability. Based on these insights, we propose DejaVu, a system that uses a low-cost algorithm to predict contextual sparsity on the fly given inputs to each layer, along with an asynchronous and hardware-aware implementation that speeds up LLM inference. We validate that DejaVu can reduce the inference latency of OPT-175B by over 2X compared to the state-of-the-art FasterTransformer, and over 6X compared to the widely used Hugging Face implementation, without compromising model quality. The code is available at https://github.com/FMInference/DejaVu.
candidates.reason: 入力ごとに必要なattention headとMLP parameterのcontextual sparsityを低コスト予測し、非同期かつhardware-awareに疎実行するDejaVuを提案する。OPT-175BでFasterTransformer比2倍超、Hugging Face実装比6倍超の推論latency短縮を品質を損なわず報告しており、LLM推論高速化を直接扱う。
candidates.library_body_check: full_text_checked: 一次arXiv本文情報でcontextual sparsity予測、asynchronous/hardware-aware implementation、OPT-175Bのwall-clock latency評価（FasterTransformer比>2x、Hugging Face比>6x）を確認。

candidates.title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
candidates.abstract: Self-attention performs well in long context but has quadratic complexity. Existing RNN layers have linear complexity, but their performance in long context is limited by the expressive power of their hidden states. We present a practical framework for instantiating sequence modeling layers with linear complexity and expressive hidden states. The key idea is to make the hidden state a machine learning model itself, and the update rule a step of self-supervised learning. Since the hidden state is updated by training even on test sequences, our layers are called Test-Time Training (TTT) layers. We consider two instantiations: TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP, whose hidden state is a linear model and a two-layer MLP respectively. We evaluate our instantiations at the scale of 125M to 1.3B parameters, comparing with a strong Transformer and Mamba, a modern RNN. Similar to Transformer, TTT-Linear and TTT-MLP can keep reducing perplexity by conditioning on more tokens, while Mamba cannot after 16k context. TTT-MLP still faces challenges in memory I/O, but shows larger potential in long context, pointing to a promising direction for future research.
candidates.reason: 隠れ状態自体を学習モデルとし、推論系列上で自己教師あり更新するTest-Time Training layerを提案する。TTT-Linear/TTT-MLPは系列長に対して線形計算量で、125M〜1.3B規模の言語モデル評価において長文脈性能を維持し、予備的システム最適化後のTTT-Linearは8K文脈でTransformerより高速となるため対象内。
candidates.library_body_check: full_text_checked: 一次arXiv論文でTTT-Linear/TTT-MLPのhidden-state update、linear complexity、125M〜1.3B評価、8K contextでTTT-LinearがTransformerより高速、TTT-MLPのmemory I/O課題を確認。
